subject: Follow-up: Logging, masking and residency requirements for Finanova POC
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Moran <elise@finanova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-11T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: POC: Logging & data handling questions

Hi Elise —

Great to connect today. Quick recap from our call and a short list of items we promised to follow up on so you can share with your security/compliance team:

1) Request/response logs
- Do you require full request/response storing for auditing, or would storing metadata and hashed request IDs suffice?
- Can you confirm whether trace IDs generated by your clients must be preserved end-to-end, or should we strip them from persisted logs?

2) Headers and sensitive fields
- We can suppress specific headers (Authorization, Cookie) at ingestion. Need to confirm if any other headers (X-Forwarded-For, custom auth headers) must be removed.

3) PII detection & redaction
- Redwood can apply regex-based and ML-based redaction at ingestion, plus configurable masking policies before writing to disk. Do you have sample payloads we can use to validate patterns?

4) Retention & deletion
- Standard hosted logs are retained for 90 days by default; Dedicated/Private deployments can customize retention and implement customer-managed deletions. Confirm your required retention window.

5) Data residency
- You mentioned EU residency for logs. We support EU-only private deployments and dedicated GPU pools in eu-west-1. Any preference between a private VPC (customer-managed) vs dedicated Redwood-hosted capacity?

6) Audit evidence
- We can produce redactable exports for SOC2 review and provide pointers to where request logs are stored.

Attachments: redwood-logging-capabilities.pdf (brief capabilities summary)

Next steps:
- Could you share the security questionnaire (if separate) and any sample request bodies?
- Propose a technical deep-dive with our security engineer next week to demo redaction and retention controls — Wed or Thu morning PT work for you?

Thanks — Rishi

From: Elise Moran <elise@finanova.com>

Date: 2026-02-12T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC: Logging & data handling questions

Thanks, Rishi — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side after a quick sync with security: 

- Retention: Our default requirement is deletion of request/response logs after 90 days. For certain regulated flows (payment card tokenization), we need 30-day retention maximum.
- Trace IDs: We cannot persist any end-user trace identifiers that could be used to reconstruct request chains across systems. That means trace IDs should be either removed or replaced with a non-reversible hash keyed to the customer (no reversible pseudonyms).
- IPs and headers: IP addresses must be masked (not stored in cleartext). We also need the ability to suppress any header on a per-route basis.
- Raw request bodies: For PII-heavy endpoints, storage is not allowed. You must be able to redact or not persist the request body at all.

We attached the latest security-questionnaire-v2.docx — most of the questions are standard but there are a few items around key management and data residency.

Also: for compliance we prefer logs to stay in EU. If you can support a dedicated eu deployment for the POC (no cross-region fallbacks for logs), that would be ideal.

Wed/Thu next week could work for a technical deep-dive. Our security engineer (Alex Kim) will join. Are you able to share who from Redwood will present the redaction pipeline?

Regards,
Elise

Elise Moran
Head of Platform Security, Finanova
elise@finanova.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elise Moran <elise@finanova.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC: Logging & data handling questions

Elise — thanks for the details. Short answers and our proposed approach: 

- Trace IDs: We can remove trace IDs at ingestion or replace them with a salted SHA-256 hash (salt scoped per-customer, stored in KMS) to make them non-reversible. If you require no reversible mapping at all, we can choose one-way hashing and rotate salts on a schedule, or drop trace IDs entirely.

- IP masking: We support CIDR-based truncation (e.g., zero-last-octet) and full IP hashing. Both options are configurable per-route.

- Header suppression: We provide a header-suppression list that operators can manage from the Console; suppression can be applied at the proxy layer before any logging.

- Request body redaction: Two approaches — (A) redact identifiable fields via ML/reg-ex rules and persist a redacted copy, or (B) do not persist bodies for specified routes (store only event metadata and a hashed request id).

- Retention: Hosted default is 90 days; for the POC we can provision a dedicated eu pool with configurable retention windows down to 0 days (ephemeral).

- Evidence and audit: We can provide redactable exports and a runbook showing where and how logs are stored. For SOC2 evidence, our security engineer can walk through the controls.

I attached a short note (redwood-pseudonymization-notes.txt) with implementation details for option choices.

Proposed attendees for the deep-dive: Soojin Lee (security engineer, Redwood), Marissa Cole (solutions tech lead), Rishi Malhotra. Proposed time: Wed 2026-02-18 10:00 PT. Please confirm and we will send a calendar invite with an agenda.

— Marissa
